ratings_why.fun: Choosing who to play last, and carrying another tribe's best unit as the Announced one, is a real shop puzzle every turn, and the fight pays it off with a visible storm.
ratings_why.distinct: Announced is a fresh shop word no tribe has; Gust itself is close to familiar start-of-combat strikes, which holds it at 7.

verdict_why: Two rules a player can't settle from the cards (does a Gust count as an attack, and when Fair-and-Foul pays) need one clear line each; the rest reads well.

points.text: Say once whether a Gust counts as an attack. The Thunderhead's "attacks or Gusts" treats them as different, but the Föhn ruling calls forced Gusts enemy attacks, so a player can't tell whether Lady High Pressure cancels enemy Gusts or Föhn's forced ones.
Mr and Mrs Fair-and-Foul flips at Start of Turn and Fair pays at Start of Turn; say whether it pays on the turn it flips. The Risks section also calls it the Weather House, so pick one name.

Old Föhn's 7 Health dies to the first big forced Gust, so the remaining two never happen against exactly the big-attacker lobbies the Ill wind build targets. Hunker or Damage Reduction during his forced Gusts would let his job happen.
The Thunderhead is the most text in the tribe; showing the Thunder count on the card and marking him "strikes last" on his slot would keep the puzzle and make it readable at a glance.
The Helm being always Announced is the best joke in the tribe; let his banner sit permanently on his slot so the second Announced unit is easy to spot.

standouts.why: The Helm who mentions his name to everyone is always Announced: lore and rule are the same thing, and it eases the tribe's main tension.
Lady High Pressure forbids anything to happen and hands the enemy's opening to your court; one read and you get it.
Sir Vane the weathercock changes sides with whatever you played last; the fickle courtier as a card.

weakest.why: Mares' Tails is a plain Gust buffer, and the name says nothing about what it does.
Red Sky at Night is a flat End of Turn buff whose weather lore doesn't show in the rule.
Old Föhn reads backwards at first glance (enemies attack him), and he usually dies before his three forced Gusts finish.

flags.note: Up to +20/+20 a fight on each Announced unit, permanently, twice with the Helm; worth the owner's eye with Sir Vane copying it.
Shutting off every enemy Start of Combat effect may feel bad to face for some tribes.
Whether his own Thunder Gusts or Gusts from a Crier count as "the first time" needs the attack/Gust line from p1.
